reviews.reason: Static review only; I ran no tests, and the measurements are yours, not verified here. No concrete issue found. (1) Prepass keeps a valid matching: each step sets left_[chosen]=v and right_[v]=chosen, frees the old mate, and increments cardinality_ only when chosen was free. Labels and budget affect speed only, so HK starting from this matching stays correct. (2) Ring buffer cannot overflow: queued vertices are distinct free rights, so pending <= right_size(); the tail wrap when all rights are free is right, and right_size()==0 returns before the buffer is used. (3) Budget is bounded: every iteration consumes deg+1 >= 1 and each relabel consumes one unit, with saturating arithmetic, so the prepass does at most 64(V+M) edge scans. Breaking on exhaustion leaves a consistent state. (4) Early exit at min(nonisolated left, nonisolated right) is a sound upper bound; matched vertices always have an edge because clear_edges clears the matching. (5) All scratch vectors are allocated before the first write to left_/right_/cardinality_, so the strong guarantee holds. graph_ is only read, so neighbors() spans stay valid. (6) HK BFS/DFS and the path flip are consistent; the mid-phase return at the bound is safe. (7) main and IO: the sentinel digit loop refills correctly at buffer boundaries, integer output reserves 22 bytes, and the static destructor flushes. Output format matches the problem.

Static review only; I ran no tests, and the timings are yours, not verified here. No concrete issue found. (1) unit_flow: level_ as parent and next_ as arc index are written before use on the path; self-loops are skipped; the path update is correct; O(n+m) with no Frame use. (2) The bad_alloc fallback is safe: all five preflow vectors are allocated before any residual or excess write, the lambdas do not allocate, and frames_ is already reserved, so Dinic continues from an unchanged feasible state. (3) Global relabel: exact sink distances, else n+2+dist-to-source, else unseen. Excess sums to limit, so Cap cannot overflow. Heights are at most 2n+1 < UINT32_MAX because n==INT_MAX is excluded. (4) The best+1 wrap on unseen is unreachable. Any vertex that can currently reach s or t was seen at the last global relabel, because new residual arcs only arise from pushes between seen vertices. So a vertex with excess always has a seen residual neighbour, and unseen is permanent. (5) Resetting the cursor only on height change is sound. Global relabel never lowers a height (exact distances dominate valid labels; source is capped at n+2). A skipped arc can therefore only become admissible after its tail's height rises, which resets the cursor. (6) Source discards excess only at height >= n+2, which under a valid labelling means no residual s-t path. The loop ends with zero excess outside the sink, so the state is a feasible flow, either maximum or equal to limit. Resumed calls are handled the same way. (7) The work budget m+n is at least 2 and uint64_t; relabel_all rebuilds the FIFO from excess, so the interrupted vertex is not lost. (8) Public signatures, ownership and add_edge rollback are unchanged. (9) main: compression mapping and output back-mapping are correct; m==0 gives a 2-vertex graph and limit 0; limit==1 routes to unit_flow; int arithmetic is within the problem limits.
